newsitem.title: INDIA: India's VSNL issue remains uncertain.
newsitem.headline: India's VSNL issue remains uncertain.

text.p: A jumbo equity offering from top Indian telecom firm Videsh Sanchar Nigam Limited (VSNL) is still awaiting the federal government's approval, banking sources said on Thursday.
"There are a couple of issues...is the ministry going to promote a primary issue along with the divestment?" said an investment banker associated with the deal.
"Are they going to have a new beauty parade or stay with the original lead managers?"
Bankers say VSNL's $650-$800 million offering of global depositary receipts (GDRs) -- India's biggest ever -- would probably be sold jointly as a government divestment and a primary offering.
This would be the state-run firm's third launch attempt in two years after two unsuccessful attempts in 1994.
Investment banks Kleinwort Benson, Jardine Fleming and Salomon Brothers are global co-ordinators to the issue.
There has been speculation that VSNL may call for fresh presentations from investment bankers but banking sources say the company is likely to keep the original co-ordinators.
